question: Why did Castiglione have to invent the Italian word sprezzatura?
answer: Because no word named what he meant: a studied carelessness that hides all effort. In The Book of the Courtier, 1528, he offers it as perhaps a new word. The paradox was the point: the courtier rehearses so that his grace looks unrehearsed, like a dancer whose practice nobody is allowed to see.
move: When something looks effortless, ask how much effort went into the look.
ask: Where do I look effortless, and who does not see the work behind it?
source: Castiglione, The Book of the Courtier, 1528
reference: Castiglione, The Book of the Courtier, trans. George Bull, Penguin Classics, 1967
